engender

en-JEN-der · verb

Hear It

What It Means

To engender is to cause, bring about, or give rise to something, usually a feeling or situation.

The viral video of the incident engendered a heated debate about privacy that lasted for weeks.

Example

Trainers know that harsh, frightening punishment tends to engender fear and resentment in a dog, not cooperation.

Engender describes what a cause produces -- usually an emotion, attitude, or situation that grows out of it naturally.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

provoke: To provoke is to draw out a strong, usually immediate reaction -- a provoked crowd shouts back on the spot. To engender works more slowly and quietly: a cause gradually gives rise to a feeling, attitude, or situation that grows out of it over time. Provoking sparks a reaction; engendering grows one.

spawn: To spawn is to produce offspring or offshoots, often many at once -- one hit film spawns sequels, imitators, and merchandise. To engender is narrower and more abstract: it gives rise to feelings, attitudes, or situations, never physical products. A gadget spawns knockoffs; a kind gesture engenders goodwill.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

prevent: to stop something from happening

suppress: to hold something back or keep it from developing

Where it sits · how directly the effect is caused

encourage → engender → trigger

encourage vs. engender: To encourage a feeling is to gently support something already taking shape, a softer influence than engendering it, which brings the feeling into existence in the first place.

trigger vs. engender: To trigger something is to set it off suddenly and directly, a sharper, more immediate cause than simply engendering it.

Build the Word

The pieces

prefix — en-: to cause, to make (Latin/French)

root — gender: to produce, to beget (Latin generare)

Put it together: Engender combines en- ('to cause, to make') with gender (from Latin generare, 'to produce or beget,' the same root behind generate and genesis) -- literally 'to cause to be produced,' which is exactly what engender means: to bring about or give rise to something.

Use the root in a new word: generate: Dad joked that the class debate generated more heat than light.

Root Check

Word Choice

Engender is a formal word almost always used for feelings, attitudes, or situations that grow out of a cause -- not for physical objects.
